name: execute_command
description: Run a shell command. Destructive, privilege-escalation, remote-shell, and network-listener commands are blocked; ordinary HTTP clients and package managers are allowed. Truncated output reports shown/total counts; narrow or page instead of rerunning variants. Failures report the exit code.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later execute_command calls in this turn:
- Long-running or interactive commands: start with `yield_time_ms`, then poll with `session_id`, send input with `write_stdin`, or end with `close_session`. Prefer this over `&` plus log-file polling.
- `sleep` is expensive: it blocks the whole turn on dead time — do not use it unless truly necessary (e.g. waiting for a server to accept connections). Prefer `session_id` polling for commands already running, or `task_wait` for subagent tasks.

command.description: Shell command for a new call. Required for a new call; omit it when polling, writing to, or closing an existing `session_id` (passing both is rejected). Long-running or interactive work should start a session with `yield_time_ms` instead of relying on the 60-300s one-shot timeout. Do not pipe interactive commands through `head`, `tail`, `grep`, or `tee`; they can wait for process exit and stall.

input.description: Optional text written verbatim to the command's stdin immediately after spawn, up to 16 KiB. Include a trailing newline for line-oriented prompts. For pty=true this is typed into the terminal: closing the writer does not send EOF, so a program that reads until EOF will wait for timeout; send `\u0004` (Ctrl-D) explicitly for that case. Do not send secrets; the text becomes part of the tool call history.

pty.description: Required: always supply this field (the call is rejected if omitted). Use true only for interactive CLIs (prompts, QR codes, full-screen UI); use false for everything else, including background commands. With `yield_time_ms`, `pty=true` starts a persistent PTY session and `write_stdin` types into it.

session_id.description: Existing command session returned by a prior `yield_time_ms` call. Omit `command` when using this; only the session that created it may poll, write, or close it.

yield_time_ms.description: Start a persistent command session and wait up to this many milliseconds for output (1-30000, default 10000). Returns a session id when the process is still running. Use this for long builds, REPLs, and multi-step interactive commands.

write_stdin.description: Bytes written verbatim to an existing session's stdin, followed by a yield. Requires `session_id`; include a trailing newline for line-oriented prompts. With `pty=true`, EOF is not implied by ending the write: send `\u0004` (Ctrl-D) if the program waits for EOF. Do not send secrets; the text becomes part of the tool call history. Do not combine with `close_session`.

close_session.description: Terminate the existing `session_id` and remove it. Requires `session_id`; do not combine with `write_stdin` or `command`. Use this for stuck processes instead of waiting for the 10-minute idle reaper.
